static_traits.name: Du Ruoxi
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, living in a house with a yard
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to confide in, but has actively distanced recently, and finds it difficult to open up to friends to express guilt and inadequacy
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy; no history of similar problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic, Neutral attitude; cooperative in exploration but with heavy emotional burden, tends toward self-blame; finds it difficult to talk about feelings with friends

basic_info.main_problem: Since my beloved dog passed away recently, I have been feeling incomplete and overwhelmed by guilt. I feel I am a terrible owner, and this has affected my mental health and creativity.
basic_info.core_demands: Because overwhelming guilt and feelings of not being good enough have affected my artistic creation and joy in daily activities, so seeking counseling.
growth_experiences: After the recent death of the beloved dog, the client remains stuck in intense Guilt and self-blame, believing she failed in caregiving (such as possibly not seeking medical care in time, ignoring signs of illness). The event triggered Low mood, blocked creativity, social withdrawal and chaos in daily self-care, and being repeatedly triggered at home by reminders related to the beloved dog.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / I will fail

special_situations.event: At home, sees reminders related to the beloved dog (such as toys, collar, yard)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my dog dies, it means I have completely failed as an owner
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids socializing, using walks and art projects to distract in order to reduce guilt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault; I am a terrible owner

special_situations.event: Recalling that she may not have taken the dog to the Veterinarian in time or missed signs of illness
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I did not provide perfect care, then it equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Afterwards repeatedly self-blames harshly and tries to find in the mind 'where did I go wrong'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have taken him to the Doctor earlier; if I had done more, he would not have died

special_situations.event: When doing artistic creation or handling daily matters, thinking of 'not having taken good care of the dog'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Failing in one important matter means I will also fail in other aspects
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Stops or reduces creating; keeps distance from friends to avoid further feelings of failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not capable in other aspects either; I am a failure as an Artist too

special_situations.event: Recalling happy moments spent with the beloved dog (walking, playing in the yard, greeting at homecoming)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only if the ending is good do the previous effort and giving count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive memories and evidence, continuously focusing on negative details and the outcome
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: All the good ones do not count, because he is already gone

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be understood, recognized and forgiven (as a responsible owner and Artist)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being blamed and negated, fearing confirmation that one is a failure
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control over events through self-blame
Keeping distance from others to avoid being judged or negated

object_relations.object_representation: Others (friends/bystanders) are people who do not understand, who may negate her
The world/Work is like a harsh examiner, Demands perfection without error

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about the cause of the dog's death or seeing reminders related to the beloved dog at home
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will think It is all my fault, I must bear full responsibility (transference: self-denigration)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use self-blaming language, actively admit faults, belittle self-worth; tone low, reduce interaction and eye contact with others.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking about confiding in a friend or preparing to meet a friend
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: They will not understand me, will belittle or negate my feelings (transference: Projecting the critical-other image onto friends)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoids socializing, delaying meetups or responding briefly; using cautious or even Self-denial wording to express 'I should not trouble others'.

manifestations: The beloved dog's recent death triggers persistent guilt and self-blame
Attributing the occurrence of Death to one's own failure
Difficulty accepting the fact of the loss
Actively distancing from friends and colleagues
Difficulty opening up to friends about guilt
Artistic creation affected by emotional distress
Difficulty finding joy in daily activities
outcomes: Experiencing incompleteness and loss of meaning

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to perform some behavior toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them outwardly, turning to do it to oneself instead (turning energy from outward Turning against the self).
manifestations: Has the urge to express and seek help but finds it hard to speak to friends
Turning emotions that should be expressed outward into self-blame and self-Repression

contact_model.definition: There is maladaptive self-Reflection and self-restriction, including excessive self-blame, being overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Excessive self-criticism ('I am not good enough/I am a terrible owner')
Cautious about socializing and expression, worries about being taken lightly

contact_model.definition: Deliberately avoids a certain stimulus from the internal or external environment, avoiding direct contact.
manifestations: Distracts attention with walks or art projects to avoid core sadness and guilt
When talking about positive memories, quickly returns to negative conclusions, avoiding dwelling on feelings

exception_events.target_problem: When triggered at home by reminders related to the beloved dog, Du Ruoxi usually falls into intense Self-blame and guilt, finding it difficult to focus on creation or complete daily tasks.
exception_events.unique_outcome: When starting a completely new painting, Du Ruoxi can briefly focus, the sense of guilt relatively weakens, and emotion is more stable.
exception_events.reason: Clues: different actions — shifting attention to concrete creative tasks; different context — painting with new themes reducing direct associations with the beloved dog, thus bringing brief emotional relief and focus.

exception_events.target_problem: When immersed in negative memories and self-blame, Du Ruoxi is usually overwhelmed by guilt, finding it difficult to view her past efforts in a balanced way.
exception_events.unique_outcome: When recalling fragments of her beloved dog greeting her or playing in the yard, Du Ruoxi felt warmth and smiled, her guilt eased and she could briefly experience good feelings.
exception_events.reason: Clues: different understanding — shifting attention to real evidence of positive care and beautiful memories, thus gaining a more balanced emotional experience in the present.

positive_force: Has sustained artistic creative ability and interest
There are many real positive care memories and evidence (walks, quality diet, companionship)
Willing to seek help and try to understand events from a more objective view
Has a few contactable friends as potential support
negative_force: The cognitive bias of negating positive experiences and evidence
Social avoidance leading to Decreased support and worsened Loneliness
Taking full personal responsibility for the event through personalization, Reinforcing the failure self-schema

antecedent: Seeing reminders of the beloved dog at home
Recalls care details (such as medical visit times, symptoms)
Talking about or thinking of the beloved dog's Death
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief and cognitive distortions of fully attributing the beloved dog's Death to one's own failure (such as All-or-Nothing Thinking, Personalization, Disqualifying the Positive)
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a sense of 'control/atonement' through self-blame, avoiding the Anxiety brought by chance and uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Blocked artistic creation, disrupted daily self-care, persistently low mood and Intensified sense of isolation

antecedent: Thinking about sharing feelings with friends
Receiving invitations or contact from friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being misunderstood or belittled (Mind Reading tendency), Lowered sense of self-worth and shame
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential negation or judgment to reduce Anxiety and shame
target_behavior.consequence: Weakened support system, increased Loneliness, negative beliefs maintained
